content_full:
To make a YouTube banner with AI, describe your channel in a prompt, upload a portrait or logo for the AI to follow, and generate the art at 16:9 and 2560 x 1440 with your name in the center safe area. Then fix any detail, download the file and upload it in YouTube Studio. The whole job takes one canvas and a few runs.

In the YouTube banner maker, you type the channel name, niche, palette and mood, and the AI designs the channel art around them. Later changes, like a new series title or date, take one Inpaint pass instead of a redesign.

This guide covers how to make a YouTube banner step by step: what to put on it, the sizes that keep it from getting cropped, six steps from prompt to upload, and how to keep every piece of channel art looking like one set.

What a YouTube channel banner is and what goes on it

A YouTube banner, also called channel art or a YouTube cover photo, is the wide image across the top of your channel page. It is often the first thing a visitor sees, so it has a few seconds to say who you are and what you post. A good one reads in a single glance, on a phone as clearly as on a TV.

Most strong channel art carries the same short list:

  • Your channel name, big and bold enough to stand out from whatever sits behind it.
  • A one-line promise about your videos, like “Weeknight dinners in 20 minutes”.
  • Your face or logo, so people recognize you from your thumbnails.
  • Your posting days, as long as you stick to them.
  • A palette shared with your thumbnails and logo, so the whole channel looks like one brand.

Each item on that list becomes a line in your prompt, which is why it pays to decide on all of them before you open the canvas.

YouTube channel banner size and safe area

The recommended YouTube banner size is 2560 x 1440 pixels, in a 16:9 frame. The smallest file YouTube takes is 2048 x 1152, with the same ratio and a 6 MB cap. Anything smaller, 1024 x 576 for example, falls under that floor.

The same file shows on every device, but each one crops it differently. TVs display the full banner, while computers, tablets and phones show only a wide strip across the middle:

To make a YouTube banner fit on all devices, park the name, logo and promise line inside that central safe area, and let the background fill the edges. At the 2048 x 1152 minimum, the safe area is 1235 x 338 pixels. The YouTube size guide lists the dimensions for thumbnails, Shorts and profile pictures too.

How to make a YouTube banner in 6 steps

Start in Picsart’s YouTube banner maker, on a blank canvas or from a ready-made workflow in Flow templates. Each generation uses the AI credits in your Picsart plan.

Step 1. Open a blank canvas

Start a new workflow on a blank canvas in Picsart Flow. Steps 2 to 5 all happen on this one canvas, from the first prompt to the finished file.

Step 2. Upload a portrait or logo

Drop in your avatar, a headshot or your logo as the reference image, so the banner carries the same face or mark your viewers already know.

Step 3. Describe your channel in the prompt

Spell out the channel name, the niche, a color palette, the mood and the promise line in the prompt. Ask for every piece of text in the middle third of the frame, so nothing gets cropped on phones.

Cooking channel banner

Wide 16:9 YouTube channel banner, 2560 x 1440. Warm kitchen scene with a wooden counter, copper pans and soft morning light from the left, slightly blurred at the edges. In the center, the channel name ‘Pan & Pantry’ in a bold rounded cream serif, with ‘Weeknight dinners in 20 minutes’ below in small terracotta caps. On the right of the title, a round portrait of the host from the reference photo. Hold every word and the portrait within the middle third of the frame. Cozy, inviting, high contrast, no other text.

Step 4. Set the size and run

Set the frame to a 16:9 ratio, pick 2560 x 1440 as the output size, then hit run. For a comparison, right-click the canvas, add a second model and give it the same prompt. Keep whichever version stays legible at small sizes.

Step 5. Fix details with Inpaint and Outpaint

Paint over the name, a date or a patch of background with Inpaint, then type the change. Only the masked area is redrawn, and the result appears as a new node beside the original. Starting from a narrow photo of yourself or your setup instead? Pick the 16:9 aspect chip in Outpaint to grow it into a full-width banner background.

Step 6. Download and upload to YouTube

Sign in to your Picsart account and download the finished banner. Next, open YouTube Studio, click Customization in the left menu, switch to the Profile tab and select Change beside the banner image. Choose your file, drag the crop until the name and logo land in the safe area, then hit Done and Publish.

Turn your channel graphics into one matching set

Channel art pulls its weight once every graphic on the page looks like they came from the same designer. In Picsart Flow, Shift-drag a single style reference onto every image node, and every connected graphic picks up the same palette and style. Build the banner and your thumbnails on one canvas, so the whole set sits side by side while you work.

Two ready-made workflows in Flow templates help round it out. Viral YouTube Thumbnails Using AI takes a host portrait and a hero dish shot and returns three 16:9 thumbnail designs, a natural match for the cooking banner above. For the channel logo, the Create Elegant Brand Logo Variations for Branding workflow takes your logo and two brand colors and returns matching lockups, a submark and a favicon in light and dark.

Channels change, and the banner should keep up. A holiday, a fresh series or new posting days only need an Inpaint pass: mask the words that changed and type what replaces them. Everything outside the mask stays pixel-identical, and the older version remains on the canvas in case you want it back.

Get answers to common questions

2560 x 1440 pixels at a 16:9 ratio. Anything below 2048 x 1152 gets rejected, files top out at 6 MB, and your name and logo belong inside the central safe area.

One banner file serves TVs, computers and phones, and each screen crops it its own way. Text near the edges gets cut off on smaller screens, so hold it to the middle band and leave the outer edges to the background.

Every generation draws on the AI credits in your Picsart plan. The canvas displays an estimate ahead of each run, so the price of a version is clear before you spend anything.

Yes. Reopen the canvas in Picsart Flow and mask any area for Inpaint, stretch the canvas outward with Outpaint, or change a node’s prompt and rerun it. Every edit creates a new node, and the original stays untouched.

Start your YouTube channel art

Learning how to make a YouTube banner that reads on every screen comes down to one clear prompt, the right size and your name in the center. Describe your channel in the YouTube banner maker and generate your first version today.
